recommendation: Keep the commit. It finishes the published FHIR-32271 requirements in current build-visible source while leaving background FHIR-30505 and retracted FHIR-39332 for their own audit paths if ever needed.
issue_request: FHIR-32271 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for OO. It requested removing DeviceDefinition.parentDevice, leaving DeviceDefinition.hasPart unchanged, explaining the DeviceDefinition versus Device hierarchy direction with examples in DeviceDefinition Notes, making no Device resource change, and ensuring search parameters were updated.
initial_application: No commit message explicitly mentioned FHIR-32271. Commit 2cfdd9c837592f22e50fa54e7d6635d5746c0397 appears to have applied the primary change by commenting out DeviceDefinition.parentDevice and the DeviceDefinition-parent search parameter. Current fhir.ini also records parentDevice as removed in favor of hasPart, but the DeviceDefinition Notes file was still empty and the build-visible FHIR ModelInfo example still exposed parentDevice while omitting hasPart.
additional_context: The OO/Devices Confluence project page records accepted Option 4: Device instances use Device.parent, DeviceDefinition uses hasPart for reusable component definitions, DeviceDefinition.parentDevice is removed, and explanatory examples should be added. FHIR-30505 introduced hasPart and supplies the rationale. FHIR-39332 was found nearby but is Resolved - No Change/Retracted for DeviceMetric and did not require a separate source decision.
reconciliation: Added DeviceDefinition Notes text explaining hasPart versus Device.parent with vital-signs monitor module examples. Updated the FHIR ModelInfo content to define DeviceDefinition.HasPart, add DeviceDefinition.hasPart, remove DeviceDefinition.parentDevice, and refreshed the embedded Library.data payload so the Library/FHIR-ModelInfo resource matches the edited model-info XML.
